Forward Planning – Report March 2026 
 
The Guidelines set out housing growth targets for Westmeath to 2040, 
requiring the delivery of 983 units per annum to 2034, 685 units per 
annum from 2035 to 2040, and an additional provision of up to 50% 
headroom above these figures. For the nine-year period 2026–2034, the 
combined target including headroom amounts to 13,275 residential units.
A review of existing zoned and permitted lands indicates that the county 
currently has capacity to deliver approximately 12,149 units, resulting in a 
projected shortfall of 1,126 units against the 2034 target. To address this, 
a phased variation programme to the County Development Plan was 
recommended in a targeted, plan-led manner aligned with the county's 
settlement hierarchy. 
Phase 1 – Mullingar: Variation 1 of the CDP was made by the Elected 
Members on 29 January 2026. This includes a new Settlement Plan for 
Mullingar with a 10-year planning horizon to 2036, providing 
approximately 114.5 hectares of proposed residential land and a further 
21.52 hectares of developable land, with capacity for approximately 4,761 
units. 
Phase 2 – Athlone: A new Settlement Plan for Athlone is being prepared 
jointly with Roscommon County Council, covering a similar 10-year 
horizon. The statutory process is scheduled to commence in May 2026. 
Phase 3 – Smaller Towns and Villages: Following completion of the 
Athlone variation, a further variation will assess and zone additional 
residential lands across a range of lower tier settlements. 
The findings and approach were presented to the Elected Members at the 
February Council meeting, where the Members endorsed the programme. 
Formal notification was also issued to the Minister for Housing.

Speed Limit Review 
 
The Road Traffic Act 2024 provides for the phased lowering of speed limits in Ireland.  
 
Phase 1.      A reduction in the default speed limit on rural local roads from 80km/h to 60km/h.   
Phase 2.      The introduction of a 30km/h speed limit in built-up and urban areas.   
Phase 3.      A reduction in the speed limit on national secondary roads from 100km/h to 80km/h. 
Phase 4.      The introduction of reduced speed limits adjacent to schools in rural areas.  
 
Phase 1 – Rural Local Roads 
 
The first phase, the change in the default speed limit on rural local roads from 80km/h to 60km/h 
commenced in 2024 and this lowered default speed limit came into effect on the 7th February 2025.   
 
In 2024, Westmeath County Council completed a review in accordance with section 9 of the Road 
Traffic Act of 2004, for our rural local roads. Following completion of this first phase review, no 
amendments to the existing byelaws were required; the new national default speed limit of 60km/h 
was applied to all our rural local roads.  
 
Phase 2 – Built-up and Urban Areas 
 
The second phase of the proposed speed limit changes concerns the introduction of a 30km/h speed 
limit in urban areas. It is intended that this speed limit change will be introduced by way of ‘special 
speed limit bye-laws, rather than a change in the ‘default speed limit’. Accordingly, in respect of those 
roads in urban areas where local authorities propose to change existing speed limits to 30km/h, it will 
be necessary for each local authority to undertake a statutory public consultation process and consider 
representations, in accordance with the requirements of the ‘Road Traffic Act 2004’, as amended. As 
the making of ‘special speed limit bye-laws is a reserved function, the speed limits on roads in urban 
areas will only be changed where a majority of the elected members vote to do so. 
 
To assist local authorities with the second phase, Chapters 4 & 7 of the ‘Guidelines for Setting and 
Managing Speed Limits in Ireland have been updated. Westmeath County Council commenced the 
review process of all built-up & urban areas in Q1 2026. Specific targets for implementation are: 
 
- 
October 30th, 2026 – Conclude the adoption of special speed limit Bye-Law process for built-
up and urban areas 
- 
March 31st, 2027 – Implementation of all urban speed limit changes 
To assist Council Members in this process, pre-draft briefing sessions were held, and further 
information will be provided in the coming days. 
 
Phase 3 – National Secondary Roads 
 
The third stage deals with our National Secondary roads. This phase requires legislative changes to 
ensure that local authorities are permitted to set a special speed limit of 100km/h on National 
Secondary roads. It is anticipated that this Bill will be enacted by year end 2026. A further Circular 
will issue from the Department of Transport to local authorities to confirm when this legislation has 
been enacted and when the review of speed limits on National Secondary roads should commence.

Phase 4 – Roads Adjacent to Schools in Urban Areas 
 
The fourth phase concerns the introduction of reduced speed limits on roads adjacent to schools in 
rural areas. The ‘Speed Limit Review’ included a recommendation that roads adjacent to schools in 
rural areas should have a special speed limit of 50km/h. A further Circular will issue from the 
Department of Transport to local authorities with details on when this review should be carried out.
